title: HCP — Context entry
description: The Human Context Protocol (HCP) 2.0-draft-3 context entry (HCP section 4) and its parts, shared by the hcp/* tasks. Written for this registry from the HCP 2.0-draft-3 specification text (CC BY 4.0, https://github.com/loyalagents/hcp-spec), with attribution; not copied from HCP's own schema files. Objects are open, as HCP's are (HCP Appendix A.3): a member HCP defines that is not declared here, or that a later draft adds, is preserved rather than rejected, so an entry round-trips intact. Only members whose shape the HCP text fixes are declared. Where this schema and the HCP text differ, the HCP text governs.

Entry.description: An HCP context entry (HCP section 4), carried verbatim. A Context Client normally receives a Disclosure, which carries a grant-scoped `ref` in place of `id` (HCP 7.4); the stable `id` reaches only the parties HCP lets see it.

schema.description: The HCP entry schema identifier the entry conforms to, as HCP defines it.

id.description: The entry's stable identifier (HCP section 4). Never disclosed to a Context Client, which sees a `ref` instead (HCP 7.4).

type.description: The entry type, as HCP defines it.

subject.description: The Context Subject the entry is about.

content.description: What the entry says, shaped by the content profile the entry uses (HCP section 4).

assertion.description: Who declared the content, how, and with what confidence (HCP 4.2.5).

classification.description: The entry's categories and purpose limits (HCP 4.5).

record.description: The entry's status, version and provenance as recorded by the provider.

evidence.description: Evidence items backing the entry, such as a verifiable credential. At most one item has role `content` (HCP section 4). Absent when the entry carries no evidence.

id.description: The subject's identifier as presented to the reader. A Context Client sees a per-client pseudonym (HCP 3.4), never an identifier shared across clients.

Content.description: Entry content. Its shape is set by the content profile: the General Context profile (`https://hcp.example/spec/profiles/general-context/2.0`) carries `value` and `language`; the VC Evidence profile points at an evidence item instead (HCP section 4).

value.description: The context itself under the General Context profile: a string, or an object whose shape the profile leaves to the entry type.

language.description: The language of `value`, as a BCP 47 language tag. Absent when the profile or value has none.

Assertion.description: How the entry's content was declared (HCP 4.2.5). HCP requires `confidence` when `declarationType` is `model-inferred`.

declarationType.description: Who declared the content: the person, a model inferring it, or an issuer attesting it. HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

confidence.description: The asserter's confidence in an inferred assertion. REQUIRED by HCP when `declarationType` is `model-inferred`; null or absent otherwise.

validUntil.description: The instant after which the assertion no longer holds. Absent when it states no end.

basis.description: What the assertion was drawn from (HCP 4.2.5): the sources (`drawnFrom`), the task, the setting and the rationale. Carried as HCP defines it.

permittedPurposes.description: Purposes the asserter permits the content to be used for. Absent when the assertion sets none.

Classification.description: The entry's classification (HCP 4.5). A grant reaches an entry when it covers any one of the entry's categories.

categories.description: The entry's categories; at least one (HCP 4.5).

dimension.description: A hint at the aspect of the person the entry describes. A hint only; it grants and limits nothing (HCP 4.5).

permittedPurposes.description: Purposes the entry may be disclosed for. Absent when the classification sets none.

Record.description: The provider's record of the entry: its status, version, provenance, relationships, conversion and metadata. Members other than `status` and `provenance` are carried as HCP defines them.

status.description: The entry's lifecycle status, as HCP defines it.

provenance.description: Who asserted the entry, under which grant it was submitted, and who recorded it.

Provenance.description: The entry's provenance (HCP section 4): `assertedBy`, `assertedAt`, `source`, `submittedByClient`, `authorizedUnder` (the grant), `recordedByProvider`, `recordedAt` and `confirmations`. The instants are declared here; the other members are carried as HCP defines them.

assertedAt.description: When the asserter made the assertion.

recordedAt.description: When the provider recorded the entry.

EvidenceItem.description: One evidence item on an entry (HCP section 4).

role.description: `content`: the item is the entry's content (VC Evidence profile). `supports`: the item backs content stated elsewhere in the entry.

type.description: The evidence type, such as `verifiable-credential`, as HCP defines it.
